reference: The parity case compares uptime -s with procps-ng uptime, which reports the integer /proc/stat btime. Fixture contracts use the documented uptime interface, hard-coded UTC encodings of fixture btime, and Bash printf's independent epoch-to-calendar-time conversion for the fallback case. Type/help metadata is checked through Bash builtins.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata, plus the documented version string
Pretty output at minute/hour boundaries and for singular/plural day forms
Fixture btime parsing after a long /proc/stat line and the missing-btime fallback
Missing uptime input, unknown option, and unexpected operand errors
exclusions: Default output is deferred because wall time, load averages, and utmp user counts cannot be fixed for both GNU uptime and the loadable in this runner.
Alternate locales, malformed proc files, and utmp session counting are not covered.

cases.purpose: Compare the stable boot timestamp from the builtin with GNU procps uptime -s; the runner fixes TZ=UTC and each side reads the same boot-time contract.
Verify Bash registers uptime as a builtin and exposes the documented usage and option descriptions through help.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t uptime) == builtin ]]
helptext=$(help uptime)
case "$helptext" in
  *"uptime [-p] [-s] [-h|--help|-V|--version]"*"-s   since: print boot timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)"*"-V   show version"*) ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac
printf 'builtin\nhelp metadata available\n'

cases.purpose: Check the version text documented by the loadable's -V option.
Check seconds below a minute, singular and plural minute labels, and the transition to one hour using small deterministic proc uptime fixtures.
cases.script:
export BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=.
printf '59.99 0.00\n' > uptime
uptime -p
printf '60.00 0.00\n' > uptime
uptime -p
printf '3599.99 0.00\n' > uptime
uptime -p
printf '3600.00 0.00\n' > uptime
uptime -p
cases.stdout:
up 0 minutes
up 1 minute
up 59 minutes
up 1 hour, 0 minutes

cases.purpose: Check day, hour, and minute fields including singular day wording and plural days with zero-valued smaller units.
cases.script:
export BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=.
printf '90061.00 10.00\n' > uptime
uptime -p
printf '172800.00 20.00\n' > uptime
uptime -p
cases.stdout:
up 1 day, 1 hour, 1 minute
up 2 days, 0 hours, 0 minutes

cases.purpose: Check default minute, hour and day forms at deterministic uptime boundaries, with the wall clock bracketed and all three fixture load averages verified.
cases.script:
export BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=. LC_ALL=C
printf '0.01 1.20 12.34 1/2 3\n' > loadavg
for spec in '0|0 min' '59|0 min' '60|1 min' '3599|59 min' '3600| 1:00' '7380| 2:03' '86400|1 day, 0 min' '93780|1 day,  2:03' '173100|2 days, 5 min' '864300|10 days, 5 min'; do
  seconds=${spec%%|*}; duration=${spec#*|}
  printf '%s.00 0.00\n' "$seconds" > uptime
  printf -v before '%(%H:%M:%S)T' -1
  row=$(uptime) || exit 1
  printf -v after '%(%H:%M:%S)T' -1
  clock=${row:1:8}
  [[ $clock == "$before" || $clock == "$after" ]] || exit 1
  tail=${row:9}
  [[ $tail == " up $duration, "* ]] || exit 1
  tail=${tail#" up $duration, "}
  [[ $tail =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\ user(s)?,\ \ load\ average:\ 0\.01,\ 1\.20,\ 12\.34$ ]] || exit 1
done
printf 'default durations, clock and loads verified\n'
cases.stdout: default durations, clock and loads verified

cases.purpose: Verify -s finds the documented btime line even when a preceding /proc/stat line exceeds 4096 bytes; the expected UTC timestamp is independently encoded from epoch 1700000000.
cases.script:
export BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=.
printf '90061.00 10.00
' > uptime
printf 'cpu 0
intr %05000d
btime 1700000000
' 0 > stat
uptime -s

cases.purpose: Exercise the documented now-minus-uptime fallback when stat has no btime; independently encode both possible enclosing wall-clock seconds with Bash printf %T.
cases.script:
export BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=.
printf '90061.99 0.00\n' > uptime
before=$EPOCHSECONDS
actual=$(uptime -s)
after=$EPOCHSECONDS
printf -v expected_before '%(%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S)T' "$((before - 90061))"
printf -v expected_after '%(%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S)T' "$((after - 90061))"
[[ $actual == "$expected_before" || $actual == "$expected_after" ]]
printf 'fallback timestamp verified\n'

cases.purpose: Check that a missing fixture uptime file fails with a diagnostic instead of reporting a plausible duration.
Check the documented usage failure for an unrecognized option.
Check the documented usage failure when an operand follows the supported options.
Compare the complete default uptime row, including wall clock, user count, and load averages.
